independent_solution: Additions need operands of the same kind and dimension; multiplications only combine dimensions. Take the textbook convention that a component A_x is a number (A_x itself is not a vector; A_x i is).

(a) 'any' two scalars may differ in dimension (mass + time) -> not meaningful in general; (b) scalar + vector has no direction to combine -> not meaningful; (e) 'any' two vectors may differ in dimension (velocity + force) -> not meaningful in general; (f) the component A_x is a scalar, so adding it to the vector A -> not meaningful.
(c) any vector times any scalar is a vector with product dimension (velocity x time = displacement) -> meaningful; (d) any two scalars multiply (dimensions multiply) -> meaningful.

Check each item for a needed direction: temperature, pressure (normal force per area, a scalar), time, power, total path length, energy, gravitational potential, coefficient of friction and charge are fully given by a signed number and unit.
Impulse = F x (time interval) = change of momentum: a vector times a scalar is a vector, so it is the only vector.
A scalar is defined only by having magnitude and no direction; test each extra property with a counterexample.

(a) False: kinetic energy (scalar) is not conserved in an inelastic collision. (b) False: temperature in deg C or work/potential energy can be negative. (c) False: mass, time, energy are scalars with dimensions. (d) False: temperature or gravitational potential varies from point to point.
(e) True: a scalar has no direction, so rotating the axes cannot change its value (only vector components change).

findings.detail: QUESTION card claim goes beyond its quote: it adds 'the answer, impulse, is a vector formed by multiplying a vector by a scalar duration', but the quote is only the exercise text of NCERT 3.3. A QUESTION card's claim must restate the question only; the answer belongs to the ANSWER_KEY card EV-PHY-11-MIP-02-010 and the rationale to a RELATION card (e.g. EV-PHY-11-MIP-02-003). Trim the claim to what the quote supports.
